Don't show this message again Close Print Real consumption per capita increases in the euro area and the EU Overview In the second quarter of 2026, household real income per capita increased by 0.1% in the euro area , after an increase of 0.1% in the first quarter of 2026. In the same period, household real consumption per capita increased by 0.3%, after having stayed stable in the previous quarter. These data come from a detailed set of seasonally adjusted quarterly European sector accounts that is published by Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union . In the EU as a whole, household real income per capita increased by 0.1% in the second quarter of 2026, after having increased by 0.3% in the first quarter of 2026. At the same time, household real consumption per capita increased by 0.4%, after a decrease of 0.1% in the previous quarter. Components of household real income During the second quarter of 2026, the slight increase in household real income per capita in the euro area is mainly explained by the positive contribution of net property income and other net current transfers while in the EU by the compensation of employees and social benefits other than social transfers in kind . Conversely, the largest negative contributor in the euro area was gross operating surplus and gross mixed income while in the EU it was current taxes and net social contributions . Household saving rate decreased both in the euro area and the EU In the second quarter of 2026, the saving rate decreased by 0.2 percentage points (pp) in the euro area and by 0.3 pp in the EU , compared with the previous quarter.
